title: Inspect Hospital Station Daily Preventive Maintenance (Barcode Scanner, Stacklight, Tabletop Debris)
summary: Perform a daily preventive maintenance inspection on each hospital station by verifying the barcode scanner is operational, the stacklight is operational, and the tabletop is free of debris (e.g., stuck labels).
when_to_use: Use this procedure for daily preventive maintenance on each hospital station to confirm the station’s barcode scanner and stacklight are operational and that the tabletop is clear of debris.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform the visual inspection at each hospital station and clear tabletop debris if possible; stop and escalate when a scanner/stacklight is not operational or debris cannot be cleared.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to each hospital station
Visual inspection capability for barcode scanner, stacklight, and tabletop

access_required: Physical access to each hospital station

visual_references.description: Hospital station photo showing the stacklight and its signal context (solid red/solid green/red-yellow-green, flashing red, flashing yellow). Use to visually identify the stacklight assembly and expected signal context during inspection.
Hospital Station layout diagram showing induct/extract sides and the location of the green barcode scanner for station context during inspection.

Tote initialization procedure image (Zebra scanner) included in the packet as scanner-related visual guidance; use only as a visual reference for the Zebra scanner workflow context if needed during escalation/maintenance discussion.

steps.title: Inspect each hospital station barcode scanner for operational condition
steps.purpose: Confirm the barcode scanner at each hospital station is operational as required for station operation.
steps.instruction: For each hospital station, visually inspect the barcode scanner to confirm it is operational (e.g., not visibly damaged/obstructed).
steps.expected_result: The barcode scanner at the station is operational (no visible damage/obstruction preventing normal use).
steps.healthy_condition: Barcode scanner appears intact and unobstructed at the hospital station.
steps.failure_condition: Barcode scanner appears damaged and/or obstructed such that it is not operational.

actions.label: Visual check scanner
actions.exact_action: Visually inspect the barcode scanner to confirm it is operational (e.g., not visibly damaged/obstructed).

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop inspection for this station if the barcode scanner is not operational.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.1.2: HOSPITAL STATION — Inspect each hospital station for: The barcode scanner is operational.

steps.title: Inspect each hospital station stacklight for operational condition
steps.purpose: Confirm the stacklight at each hospital station is operational as required for station status indication.
steps.instruction: For each hospital station, visually inspect the stacklight to confirm it is operational (e.g., not visibly damaged/obstructed).
steps.expected_result: The stacklight at the station is operational (no visible damage/obstruction preventing normal use).
steps.healthy_condition: Stacklight assembly appears intact and unobstructed at the hospital station.
steps.failure_condition: Stacklight appears damaged and/or obstructed such that it is not operational.

actions.label: Visual check stacklight
actions.exact_action: Visually inspect the stacklight to confirm it is operational (e.g., not visibly damaged/obstructed).

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop inspection for this station if the stacklight is not operational.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.1.2: HOSPITAL STATION — Inspect each hospital station for: The stacklight is operational.

Figure 3-5: Hospital Station Stacklight — stacklight signal context includes Solid Red (Default/Indeterminate), Solid Green (No AGV present), Red/Yellow/Green (RMS error), Flashing Red (Fault), Flashing Yellow for 15 seconds (AGV present at either position).

steps.title: Inspect tabletop and clear debris (e.g., stuck labels)
steps.purpose: Ensure the tabletop at each hospital station is free of debris that could interfere with tote handling.
steps.instruction: For each hospital station, inspect the tabletop and remove/clear any debris such as stuck labels.
steps.expected_result: The tabletop is free of debris (no stuck labels) at the station.
steps.healthy_condition: Tabletop surface is clear of debris/stuck labels.
steps.failure_condition: Debris (e.g., stuck labels) remains on the tabletop after attempted clearing.

actions.label: Check tabletop
actions.exact_action: Inspect the tabletop and remove/clear any debris such as stuck labels.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop inspection for this station if debris cannot be cleared.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.1.2: HOSPITAL STATION — Inspect each hospital station for: The tabletop is free of debris.

steps.title: Stop inspection and escalate when scanner/stacklight/debris issue is found
steps.purpose: Prevent continued operation with an impaired station and route the issue to maintenance support.
steps.instruction: If a hospital station barcode scanner or stacklight is not operational, or if debris cannot be cleared, stop the inspection for that station and escalate to the appropriate maintenance contact.
steps.expected_result: Inspection is stopped for the affected station and maintenance escalation is initiated.
steps.healthy_condition: All stations inspected successfully with no unresolved scanner/stacklight/debris issues.
steps.failure_condition: Continuing inspection/operation despite an unresolved scanner/stacklight issue or remaining tabletop debris.

actions.label: Escalate maintenance
actions.exact_action: Stop the inspection for any station where the barcode scanner or stacklight is not operational or where debris cannot be cleared, and escalate to the appropriate maintenance contact.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.1.2: HOSPITAL STATION — Inspect each hospital station for: The barcode scanner is operational; The stacklight is operational; The tabletop is free of debris.

success_criteria: For every hospital station inspected: barcode scanner is operational.
For every hospital station inspected: stacklight is operational.
For every hospital station inspected: tabletop is free of debris (no stuck labels).
healthy_conditions: Barcode scanner at each hospital station is operational (not visibly damaged/obstructed).
Stacklight at each hospital station is operational (not visibly damaged/obstructed).
Tabletop at each hospital station is free of debris (e.g., stuck labels).
failure_conditions: Any hospital station barcode scanner is not operational.
Any hospital station stacklight is not operational.
Any hospital station tabletop still has debris (e.g., stuck labels) after clearing attempt.
escalation_guidance: If a hospital station barcode scanner or stacklight is not operational, or debris cannot be cleared, stop inspection for that station and escalate to the appropriate maintenance contact.
If the maintenance issue is related to the tipper, contact Lifecycle Performance Services (LPS) at 888-444-4647.

missing_details: The manual section provided defines “operational” for the barcode scanner and stacklight at a high level (operational / not visibly damaged/obstructed) but does not specify exact pass/fail indicators beyond that; the candidate requested additional images for what “operational” looks like for the barcode scanner and tabletop debris, but those specific images are not present in the packet as dedicated scanner/debris visuals.

The candidate includes an escalation image note about initializing totes at the sorter using a Zebra scanner; the packet does not provide a step-by-step escalation procedure for hospital-station inspection failures, so this runbook only includes the escalation instruction at a high level and the tipper-related contact number.
